key_insight: MamaBench shows that medical LLMs can look accurate on standard benchmarks yet still fail when presented with clinically similar counterfactual cases that need different answers.
clinical_relevance: For maternal and pediatric diagnosis support, this means robustness—not just top-line accuracy—must be tested before relying on LLM outputs in care settings.
method: Bias Trap Rate (BTR) plus Evidence-Anchored RAG with parameter extraction, coverage auditing, and contrastive sub-queries
evidence_signal: Across eight model/configuration setups, base accuracy overstated robust accuracy by 16–28 percentage points; EA-RAG reached 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy on Claude Sonnet 4.6.
watch_item: The remaining ~20% BTR suggests counterfactual robustness is still incomplete, so retrieval improvements should be validated carefully before clinical deployment.
paper_title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
